There's a key detail to the all-new Apple Upgrade Program: "If you're leasing an iPhone, you must connect to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when you sign up."

Daring Fireball's John Gruber has a possible explanation for that in a new article today.

The iPhone Restriction With Apple Upgrade

According to an email sent to Gruber by a former member of Apple's carrier team, the requirement stems primarily from deals Apple made with Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile in the United States.

The deals struck by Apple with each carrier are "worth hundreds of millions of dollars," and in exchange for those payments, Apple has made concessions. Requiring that an iPhone purchased through Apple Upgrade be connected to a T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T account appears to be one such concession.

The former Apple employee elaborated on the details of those deals:

There are also fraud and risk assessment considerations involved. A different former Apple Store retail employee told Gruber that fraudulent iPhone sales have "increased dramatically" since Apple began offering carrier financing at its retail stores.

Apple does note that while you need to connect the iPhone to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when you sign up for Apple Upgrade, the phone remains unlocked: "When leasing an iPhone, you must select a qualified carrier (but not a prepaid carrier plan). Leased iPhones are always unlocked, so you can switch to any other carrier at any time, subject to the terms of your selected carrier."

You can read Gruber's full article at Daring Fireball.
